WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW   What you already know
Under IFRS you call it the statement of financial position, and many IFRS balance sheets put noncurrent assets first. U.S. companies usually start with current assets and list them in order of liquidity: cash first. The rules for classifying debt are also different, as Section 2.3 shows.

LANGUAGE FOCUS   Reading a balance sheet heading
as of December 31, 2025 or at December 31, 2025: a balance sheet is always at a date, never for the year.
net of: the amount after a contra account, as in receivables, net of allowance.
issued and outstanding: shares the company has sold and still has in the hands of shareholders.

Answers and explanations are at the end of the chapter.

EXAM TRAP   Working capital or the ratio?
Paying a supplier in cash reduces current assets and current liabilities by the same amount: working capital does not change, but the current ratio changes.
Reclassifying debt from current to noncurrent increases working capital and the current ratio.
Use the operating cycle only when it is longer than one year.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: classifying three Orontes items
Step 1. Next year's installment on long-term debt, $400,000. It is due within one year, so it is a current liability; the rest of the debt stays noncurrent.
Step 2. The delivery van held for sale, $46,000. Orontes expects to sell it within the year, so it is a current asset, outside PP&E.
Step 3. The equity-method investments, $1,807,000. Orontes plans to hold them for the long term, so they are noncurrent assets.
Check. Each answer uses the same test: will the item be turned into cash, used up or settled within one year (Orontes's cycle is shorter)?

● IFRS CONTRAST   IFRS looks only at the reporting date
IAS 1 asks one question: at the reporting date, does the company have a right to defer settlement for at least twelve months? A waiver or refinancing obtained after the reporting date does not count. U.S. GAAP counts events up to the date the statements are issued. Figure F02-06 compares the two frameworks.
Short-term debt refinanced long-term after year-end, before issuance
Current (no right to defer at the reporting date)
Covenant broken at year-end; waiver for more than 12 months obtained after year-end
Covenant broken at year-end; waiver obtained on or before year-end
Covenant tested only after year-end (future compliance doubtful)
Current only if acceleration is probable
Ignored unless it removes the right to defer

WATCH: NOT YET TESTABLE   No change to debt classification
The FASB proposed a simpler debt-classification rule in 2017 and again in 2019, but removed the project from its agenda in April 2021. The rules in this section are still current. Do not use the old proposal on the exam.

EXAM TRAP   Debt traps
Refinanced after year-end but before issuance: noncurrent under U.S. GAAP, current under IFRS.
Due on demand: always current.
A waiver obtained before issuance, for more than a year: noncurrent under U.S. GAAP.

SC2-5  A five-year loan is repaid in equal annual installments. At year-end, how is the next installment classified?
A.	As a noncurrent liability
B.	As a current liability

SC2-6  At December 31 a company breaks a loan covenant, so the loan is payable on demand. On January 15, before the statements are issued, the bank gives an 18-month waiver. How is the loan classified under IFRS?
A.	Noncurrent
B.	Current under IFRS only if the bank is expected to demand payment
C.	Split between current and noncurrent
D.	Current
Answers and explanations are at the end of the chapter.
Accrue a liability and a loss (best estimate; if no best estimate, the minimum of the range)
Disclose the nature and an estimate (or say it cannot be estimated)
Never recognized before it is realized

● IFRS CONTRAST   Provisions under IAS 37
IFRS records a provision when a loss is more likely than not, a lower threshold than the U.S. 'probable'. When the estimate is a range, IFRS usually uses the midpoint; U.S. GAAP uses the best estimate or, if none, the minimum.

FALSE-FRIEND ALERT   Reserve, provision, allowance
Arabic مخصص can mean an allowance (a contra-asset), a provision (a liability) or even a reserve in equity (احتياطي). In U.S. GAAP answers, use allowance for contra-assets, accrued liability or loss contingency for liabilities, and never call either a reserve.

D.	Does nothing until next year
Answers and explanations are at the end of the chapter.

EXAM TRAP   Book value is not market value
Total stockholders' equity is a book amount. It is not what the company is worth, and it is not the market value of the shares.
